headlines.text: Flash back to 2026, when Darby Allin vs. Kevin Knight went to battle over the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.19 ? an excellent showing. Fresh off saving Kevin Knight from an MJF beatdown the week before, Allin turned away his third different World Title challenger in as many weeks in another hard-fought battle.

Rewind to 2020, when Matt Hardy made a statement, debuting in the main event in a Falls Count Anywhere match, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.34 ? a fantastic contest. Matt Hardy's AEW in-ring debut, spiraling into a wild, roaming brawl through the stadium ? Hardy switched personas mid-match, got locked in an ice machine, and fought through an ATM and a golf cart chase, a chaotic preview of the Stadium Stampede war to come.

2022 brought us this moment: Konosuke Takeshita made a statement, debuting in the main event against Jay Lethal, appearing on Rampage, rated 7.28 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle. Takeshita's official AEW television debut, stepping in against Jay Lethal on short notice ? a strong first showing that made clear the Japanese star had real staying power in AEW, even in a losing effort.

secondaries.text: On this day in 2026, Gunns & Ace made a statement, debuting in the main event as a team, appearing on Collision, rated 7.04 ? a well-worked match.
On a Friday in 2022, back when it was the first-ever encounter between Riho and Yuka Sakazaki on Rampage, rated 7.30 ? a good, competitive contest.
On this day in 2026, Cameron & Shirakawa touched down in AEW for the first time as a team, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.02.
